messages.subject: incorporating Javascript into Shiny
parts:
I am trying to learn a little Javascript, to add functionality to my Shiny apps.  I seem to be missing something fundamental in how that is done.

Why does, for instance, this line of code:

condition="$('div#plot').hasClass('recalculating') || $('div#plot').hasClass('calculating')",
    img(src="dogfetcher2.gif"), h5("fetching data; please wait...")

work just fine (executes expected behavior) and this line:

 plotclasses <- "($('div#plot').attr("class"))"

Does not?  The first line is from an example from this board, the second line, I am simply parroting the syntax of the first line, for a Javascript line of code from
a Stackoverflow question (http://stackoverflow.com/questions/1227286/get-class-list-for-element-with-jquery) .. none of the provided examples in that
thread work for me with the above syntax (I'm referring to the quotes, and the div#plot referencing the outputPlot element in this case).   With or without
the closing quotes or brackets, I get an error from Shiny when I run the app. 

Can anyone please tell me what I'm doing wrong, here.

messages.author: 129e07bdb789652f
messages.subject: Re: incorporating Javascript into Shiny
parts:
Are you trying to store a javascript variable into an R variable ? You cannot do this so easily

Your first example works because it generates html code:

> conditionalPanel
function (condition, ...) 
{
    div(`data-display-if` = condition, ...)
}

messages.subject: Re: incorporating Javascript into Shiny
parts: I can see one issue with this line:
You're using double quotes around "class", which has the effect of breaking up the string. You probably want single quotes:

On a more general note, it's not clear from the code snippet how plotclasses is being inserted into the page, and that matters - you can't put Javascript just anywhere.

-Winston
